items.subtitle: Global temperatures may continue to rise even after human CO₂ emissions stop.
items.feedText: The temperature change that follows is known as the zero emissions commitment (ZEC), and it is often assumed to be close to zero. A study led by the Met Office Hadley Center, with co-authors from several institutions including the University of Liverpool, found that the temperature response depends on how much warming has already occurred.

items.articleBody:
GIO TIROTTO DESIGNs LA LENTA BENCH FOR LIGURIA’S COAST

Developed by slow-living platform Vita lenta, Italian designer Gio Tirotto, and B Corp-certified seaside restaurant La Marinella, La Lenta is a public bench conceived to counter defensive urban furniture and restore prolonged seating to shared spaces. Scheduled for installation in spring 2027 in San Terenzo, a village in Lerici along Liguria’s Gulf of Poets, in collaboration with the Municipality of Lerici, the seating piece will sit along the waterfront facing the sea as an open-access civic amenity.

all images ©Raoul Ventura

La Lenta ELONGATES typical domestic CHAIR PROPORTIONS

Designer Gio Tirotto’s concept merges domestic and civic typologies, structured formally as an elongated chair that stretches into a bench while retaining the proportions and ergonomic detailing of indoor seating. Eliminating hostile elements such as central dividers or steeply inclined planes, the bench is engineered for both outdoor public environments and residential interiors. Its structural frame is fabricated from marine-grade AISI 316 stainless steel, paired with a seat and backrest constructed from okoumé plywood finished with a teak veneer to resist salt spray, weathering, and coastal storms.

A dedicated plaque features hand-drawn lettering by artist Loris Lillo, designer of the Vita lenta logo. Marking the first physical object produced by Vita lenta, founded by Gianvito Fanelli in 2020 as a digital platform before expanding into publishing and music, the San Terenzo installation serves as a prototype for a wider rollout of public benches across Italy, with the team seeking an industrial partner for serial production.

items.articleBody:
**Apple hat unlängst die Termine für die Swift Student Challenge 2027 bekannt gegeben. Wie schon in den Vorjahren nennt der iPhone-Konzern die Eckdaten seines Programmierwettbewerbs für Nachwuchsentwickler gut drei Monate vorher. Eingereicht wird vom 8. bis zum 28. Februar 2027.**

## Es gibt eine wichtige Änderung

Wichtiger als der Termin ist eine Änderung, auf die viele schon lange gewartet haben. Bisher waren die Einreichungen auf App Playgrounds beschränkt, die sich vor allem an iPhone und iPad richteten. Jetzt ist jede Apple-Plattform erlaubt, von macOS über watchOS bis zu tvOS und visionOS. Auch normale Xcode-Projekte nimmt Apple nun an. Nötig sind dafür Xcode 27 oder Swift Playground 4.7 oder eine neuere Version. Kommandozeilen-Tools und Swift-Pakete gelten nicht als Einreichung. Außerdem steigt das Größenlimit für das ZIP-Archiv von 25 auf 500 MB, und damit haben auch 3D-Inhalte oder aufwendigere Medien endlich Platz.

Die Grundregeln bleiben gleich. Das Projekt muss sich in höchstens drei Minuten erleben lassen, komplett offline laufen und auf Englisch sein. Eine Jury wählt die Gewinner nach Innovation, Kreativität, gesellschaftlicher Wirkung oder Inklusion aus. In Deutschland müsst ihr mindestens 16 Jahre alt sein, in Österreich und der Schweiz reichen 13. Außerdem müsst ihr eingeschrieben sein, etwa an einer Schule oder Hochschule, oder euren Abschluss erst vor Kurzem gemacht haben. Kosten fallen keine an.

## Apple bietet wieder Starthilfe an

Bis zum Start bietet Apple drei kostenlose Online-Sessions unter dem Namen „Meet with Apple“ an. Am 10. Dezember geht es um das Programmieren mit KI-Assistenten, am 14. Januar um die Challenge selbst und am 4. Februar darum, wie ihr eure App überzeugend präsentiert. Für die Besten wartet wie gewohnt eine Reise nach Cupertino. Die sogenannten Distinguished Winners verbringen drei Tage im Apple Park und erleben dort die WWDC 2027. Im vergangenen Jahr gab es 350 Gewinner aus 37 Ländern, 50 von ihnen waren vor Ort dabei. Wann die Entwicklerkonferenz stattfindet, hat Apple noch nicht verraten, meist ist es Anfang Juni.

items.title: Fighters vs. uniters and the big blue future
items.subtitle: Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama at their Jan.
items.feedText: 31, 2008 debate in Los Angeles. David McNew/Getty Images. As you may know, I’m fond of finding different ways to classify Democrats. Usually, this concerns the party’s voters, but in a New York Times story out this morning, I turned to their candidates. I have no problem with dividing the candidates into progressives and moderate “lanes,” particularly if one recognizes it as a spectrum rather than a strict boundary. But after spending a bunch of time last week binge-watching videos, debates, press appearances, a…
items.articleBody:
Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama at their Jan. 31, 2008 debate in Los Angeles. David McNew/Getty Images.

As you may know, I’m [fond](https://www.natesilver.net/p/what-is-heather-cox-richardsonism) of finding different ways to classify Democrats. Usually, this concerns the party’s voters, but in a [New York Times story out this morning](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/opinion/nate-silver-democrats-midterms-president.html), I turned to their candidates.

I have no problem with dividing the candidates into progressives and moderate “lanes,” particularly if one recognizes it as a spectrum rather than a strict boundary. But after spending a bunch of time last week binge-watching videos, debates, press appearances, and ads from 27 Democratic candidates — 13 leading 2028 contenders, plus 13 candidates who made major breakthroughs on Nov. 31, plus Zohran Mamdani2 — I don’t think that really captures the whole story.

Instead, there’s another distinction that I call “fighter” vs. “uniter.”

Graphic by the New York Times; ratings by Nate Silver.

It really does help to watch the candidates in action to see this. Some classifications are obvious. Gavin Newsom’s whole thing is to fight back by any means necessary. When it came to leading Democratic efforts to fight Republican redistricting, I [thought that was smart](https://www.natesilver.net/p/democrats-can-win-the-redistricting). I could do without his Trump-style tweeting, but I can understand why some voters like it.

While “fighter” is correlated with “progressive,” the relationship is far from perfect. I consider Zohran to be a hybrid of “fighter” and “uniter,” but he’s closer to the latter end of the spectrum and often finds a way to [signal](https://www.politico.com/news/2025/10/15/mamdani-apology-nypd-00610378) that he wants to be a mayor for all New Yorkers, including through his consummately well-presented appearance.

Conversely, I expected Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear to be fairly mild-mannered, and he often is, but look at him talking about JD Vance:

There were a lot of cases like this. I classified only Kansas Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton as a *pure* uniter, a 7 on my 7-point scale. But you can watch someone like Mary Peltola get more and more worked up in her Oct. 15 [debate against Dan Sullivan](https://www.pbs.org/video/debate-for-the-state-2026-us-senate-n8szip/), for instance. In her opening statement, she described herself affably as a “lifelong Alaskan, a mother, a grandmother” — but by 10 minutes in, she’d gotten under his skin — and him under hers. “Dan, you should be ashamed of yourself for propagating these lies,” she said.

Subscribe now

I don’t want to preempt the NYT story too much, so [go check it out](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/opinion/nate-silver-democrats-midterms-president.html). An undercurrent is simply how skilled some of the Class of 2026 are at communication. While James Talarico is perhaps the most obvious example of someone who can blend “fighter” and “uniter” styles, you’re seeing a lot of creative ways to bridge the gap, from Scott Colom’s [use of humor](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/us/elections/scott-colom-mississippi-senate-protein-ad.html) to South Carolina Sen.-elect Annie Andrews playing the “I’m just a working mom and pediatrician” card in one commercial to some [incredibly vicious attacks](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DWUak5FJy2R/?hl=en) on the late Lindsey Graham (when he was originally her opponent) in another.

#### Why “uniter” may be a more natural gear for Democrats

One thing I talked through with my editor, but we didn’t really have space to fit into the piece, is whether one strategy is likely to be more correlated with winning, either in the general election or the primary.

I thought it was clear enough that the 2028 candidates (or their consultants) are mostly moving in the fighter direction. In recent speeches, Jon Ossoff’s rhetoric has been [extremely sharp and unforgiving toward Republicans](https://www.nytimes.com/video/opinion/100000011267049/vance-was-wrong-about-ossoffs-campaign.html). He still has something of an Obama-esque cadence, but unlike most of the other candidates who are accused of this (Pete Buttigieg, Josh Shapiro, Wes Moore) he doesn’t tilt toward the “uniter” end of the scale. His rhetoric was more like Newsom’s instead.

Obama’s shadow does loom over the field, however. His 2008 primary battle against Hillary Clinton was a pretty good example of “fighter” vs. “uniter,” and the uniter won — and then went on to capture 365 electoral votes that November.

Nor, despite nearly all Democrats saying they want to fight back harder against Trump in polls, does that necessarily match Democrats’ revealed preferences in primaries. Talarico’s win over Jasmine Crockett was a strike against Team Fighter, for instance.

And there’s an asymmetry between the parties that might make the “uniter” style more natural for Democrats.

Here’s a crazy stat I came across the other day. Since 2008, Democrats have won a Senate race in *43 states*. Kansas, Maine3, Mississippi, South Carolina and Texas were added to the list this year.

This includes 13 states where Democrats haven’t won an electoral vote any time this century. Here is the same map for Republicans:

Visually, it still looks fairly impressive thanks to the presence of all those big square states in the middle of the country. But the GOP map is much patchier, with 15 states missing4 including the entire West Coast and most of the Northeast. Moreover, there’s a much closer overlap between where the GOP wins Senate seats and where they’re competitive in the presidency.

Classically in American politics, Democrats are the “big tent” coalition. They were the party of manual laborers, but also college professors, Black voters and most immigrant groups. Throughout almost all of recent American history, Democrats have led Republicans in party identification — though their lead used to be much larger before the [Solid South turned red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_South). (Although the South wasn’t so red *this* year.)

But, obviously, it’s not as though Democrats have monopolized American politics during this time. Since Jan. 1, 1940, through today, Democrats have controlled the presidency 52 percent of the time, about as close to even as it gets.

However, they’ve controlled the Senate 67 percent of the time and the House 68 percent during the same period. A lot of that came during the Solid South era of conservative, Southern Democrats. Still, the final two years of Trump’s term will widen that president vs. Congress gap. In some ways, it’s a throwback.

What accounts for the difference? Well, some of it is that Democrats’ breadth and diversity is more of a strength when they can curate candidates for individual states and districts instead of having to pick one for the whole country. With one or two exceptions5, the Democrats who won big on Nov. 3, from El-Sayed to Peltola to Colom, were very distinctively products of their respective states.

So the question is: while everyone likes a fighter, who or what are they fighting for, exactly? El-Sayed is a “fighter,” but so, unquestionably, was Haley Stevens.

Even the red state Democrats who won this year spoke with plenty of fire and conviction about high prices, about corruption, and against billionaires like Elon Musk. Those are likely to be winning themes in the presidential nomination as well as being advantages for Democrats in November 2028. Some of those same Democrats, though — like Gina Hinojosa, who actually has a fairly progressive record in the Texas state legislature — were going out of their way to reject the “culture wars.” Some featured Trump prominently but others did not — and this is trickier than you might think to navigate for 2028 since Trump himself won’t be on the ballot.

Plus, the Democratic Party has a lot of racial, class, age, religious and gender differences to bridge. (You don’t have to be woke to recognize that how candidates are perceived by voters is mediated by their race, gender and appearance.6) Sometimes, the Democrats who are urging “fight, fight, fight” can mistake the party’s online, liberal/progressive activist base for the broader base that the party really needs to win, including voters of color and many churchgoing Americans.

So I’ll cast a tentative vote for “uniter” being slightly underrated. Either way, though, go watch some of these candidates in action, especially the Class of 2026. Moving past the era of the Clintons and the Bidens [and the Cuomos](https://www.natesilver.net/p/zohran-delivered-the-democratic-establishment) and [even the Janet Millses](https://www.natesilver.net/p/democrats-are-not-ok-with-boomers) has opened up space for Democrats who are far more modern and effective communicators. Democrats really do have a lot of talent on their hands.

Silver Bulletin is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a subscriber.

1

No, there isn’t much overlap between these groups. It’s *very* rare for someone to win a major statewide office for the first time and then immediately turn around to run for president.

2

Zohran is not in the “Class of 2026” since he was elected mayor last year, and he’s not a 2028 contender since he’s a naturalized citizen and therefore isn’t eligible to be president.

3

If you don’t count Angus King, an independent who caucuses with the Democrats.

4

15 includes Michigan, which Trump won twice but where Republicans haven’t elected a Senator any time recently.

5

Annie Andrews struck me as someone who was speaking to more of a national audience, although that may be partly because she was making appeals for donor money.

6

As I said in the NYT story, there are a conspicuously large number of good-looking Democrats among the party’s rising stars.

items.feedText: The finding, published in Scientific Reports, provides a new perspective on the early manifestation of rodent gigantism—the process by which animals evolve to become larger—demonstrating that the evolutionary history of large-bodied rodents is considerably older and more geographically widespread than previously recognized, the researchers said.
items.articleBody: An international team of paleontologists, including researchers from McGill University, has discovered "remarkably large" rodent fossils in the pit of a mine in southern Thailand. The finding, published in Scientific Reports, provides a new perspective on the early manifestation of rodent gigantism—the process by which animals evolve to become larger—demonstrating that the evolutionary history of large-bodied rodents is considerably older and more geographically widespread than previously recognized, the researchers said.

items.articleBody:
For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out.

## What is T. Coronae Borealis?

[T. Coronae Borealis](https://www.space.com/stargazing/a-new-star-could-finally-appear-in-the-night-sky-this-week-thanks-to-a-once-in-a-lifetime-explosion) — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to [1,000 times its usual brightness](https://www.denverastro.org/the-2024-t-corona-borealis-t-crb-nova/) before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle.

## Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare?

"T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued.

Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached [Earth](https://www.space.com/54-earth-history-composition-and-atmosphere.html) in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth.

An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab)

"The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold."

Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event.

"There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the [Goddard Spaceflight Center](https://www.space.com/goddard-space-flight-center.html), told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption."

Hays notes that the intense light from the red giant dramatically outshines the dimmer white dwarf, making detailed observation challenging. There is also no way to precisely measure the temperature and pressure of the matter lurking near the surface of the smaller star. "Predicting nova explosions are a little like predicting the weather; conditions may be right but the timing of the storm can be uncertain."

## What will happen when T CrB's nova light reaches Earth?

There'll be no visual warning of the eruption before it reaches Earth, though according to Hays there could be an early flash of light in the X-ray spectrum.

"The world's amateur astronomers have been doing an awesome job of keeping T CrB under hair-trigger monitoring roughly every minute or two, so when T CrB has brightened by around one [magnitude](https://www.space.com/21640-star-luminosity-and-magnitude.html), then alerts will spread around the world within minutes," said Schaefer.

Once the call goes out, telescopes and observatories around the world will kick into gear, running pre-prepared observation programmes to capitalize on the rare and cataclysmic event. "When the nuclear runaway process starts, it will take off and peak very quickly, in less than a day."

The nova will see the star jump from its normal brightness of magnitude +10 — which is beyond the detection limit of the naked eye — to magnitude +1.7, making it appear as if a star brighter than the North Star [Polaris](https://www.space.com/15567-north-star-polaris.html) has suddenly burst to life in the night sky.

"The brightness will fall below naked-eye visibility in dark places within a couple of days and become too faint for binoculars within about a week," said Hays. "Outside the visible band, for example, in radio, X-ray and [gamma rays](https://www.space.com/gamma-rays-explained), light caused by the eruption will be visible for months or even years. "

## Where can I find the Blaze Star in the night sky?

T CrB can be found glowing close to the magnitude +4.28 star Epsilon Coronae Borealis in the constellation Corona Borealis during the early evening in November, with the constellations of Hercules and Bootes on either side.

Corona Borealis forms a crown-like pattern of stars between the more famous constellations of Bootes and Hercules. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva)

It will dip below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. just a few hours after sunset, before re-emerging into the northeastern sky in the predawn hours.

How to find T.CrB near Epsilon Coronae Borealis. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva)

Want to capture a photo of T. CrB when it erupts? Then be sure to read our [guide to photographing the night sky](https://www.space.com/astrophotography-for-beginners-guide), along with our picks of the [best cameras](https://www.space.com/best-cameras-for-astrophotography), [lenses](https://www.space.com/best-lenses-for-astrophotography) and [smart telescopes](https://www.space.com/best-smart-telescopes) that are perfect for capturing the majesty of the starry realm.

items.articleBody:
Mexican design studio Arudeko has developed Bianni, a paper-like material made from colourful waste wool, which can be sculpted into everything from lampshades to room dividers.

Sourced from the off-cuts of handmade carpets and cushions crafted by local weaving communities in Teotitlán del Valle, Mexico, Arudeko saw the potential to use the surplus material and save it from being discarded.

Bianni is a paper-like material crafted from colourful waste wool

Photographs

Previous

Next

Photographs

Close

The material can be sculpted into lampshades

The customisable textile – named Bianni – was made by weaving together wool with recycled paper.

Skilled local artisans initially wove the discarded dyed wool onto a pedal loom, then, using cotton threads, wove strips of recycled paper crafted by local papermakers into the material.

The result is a translucent, flexible textile that can be crafted into diverse objects, from lampshades to decorative headboard panels, room dividers and wall art.

"Through exploring the material's qualities, we discovered its potential, particularly the way light revealed colours that had been hidden within the paper, almost like a secret waiting to be uncovered," Arudeko co-founder and CEO Denisse Arnaiz told Dezeen.

"Once the paper was woven, I began observing how it behaved as a textile," added Arnaiz.

"Its translucency was what ultimately inspired us to explore its use in lighting. However, the material has many other possible applications."

Arudeko saw the potential in using surplus wool and saved it from being discarded

Arudeko has breathed new life into the surplus material

With Bianni, Arudeko aimed to uncover the hidden value of discarded wool whilst reimagining the ancient material's ancestral history and "cultural memory".

"Bianni was born from the idea of giving new life to the leftover wool from our rug and cushion production in Oaxaca," said Arnaiz. "This wool carries within it the knowledge of the artisans who work with it, as well as the colours of the earth embedded in its fibres."

Arnaiz explained that the material is made purely from natural materials, with no additives.

"No additives, just natural materials – why mix these fibres?" she said. "Not only for an aesthetic purpose, as wool brings fire resistance to the paper."

Throughout the process, the studio aimed to minimise water consumption and carbon dioxide production as much as possible. Bianni's production was also kept local to reduce transport needs whilst supporting the local community.

Read:

Harvard University transforms waste wool into cladding for retrofits

Other wool projects recently featured on Dezeen include waste-wool cladding designed for retrofits and a collection of rugs with architectural designs.

items.articleBody:
**Apple hat seine App Einladungen erneut aktualisiert und macht die Planung von Feiern damit ein gutes Stück einfacher. Neben einer praktischen Neuerung gibt es eine kleine optische Spielerei. Bislang hatten Gastgeber in Apple Einladungen keine Möglichkeit, ihre Gäste nach ihrer Meinung zu fragen. Wer wissen wollte, ob lieber gegrillt oder bestellt werden soll oder welches Motto die Party bekommt, musste dafür auf WhatsApp, iMessage oder eine separate Umfrage-App ausweichen. Mit Version 1.13 ändert sich das, denn die Abstimmung findet jetzt direkt in der Einladung statt.**

## Apple Einladungen 1.13 bekommt Umfragen für Gäste

Gastgeber können ihrer Veranstaltung nun eine Umfrage hinzufügen, über die alle Eingeladenen abstimmen. Apple nennt als Beispiele das Motto und das Menü, die Frage lässt sich allerdings frei formulieren. Damit klärt sich auch, welcher Termin den meisten passt oder welche Aktivität auf dem Programm stehen soll. Gerade jetzt vor der Saison der Weihnachtsfeiern dürfte das vielen Hosts eine Menge Hin und Her im Gruppenchat ersparen.

Dazu kommt ein neuer Emoji-Effekt. Gastgeber wählen ein Emoji passend zum Anlass, das anschließend animiert über die Einladung schwebt. Das ergänzt die bisherigen Gestaltungsoptionen wie eigene Fotos, verschiedene Schriftarten und Hintergründe aus Image Playground. Anbei die Release-Notes:

- Gastgeber können einer Einladung jetzt eine Umfrage hinzufügen und Gäste über Details wie Motto, Menü oder andere offene Punkte abstimmen lassen. Zusätzlich lässt sich ein Emoji-Effekt passend zur Stimmung der Veranstaltung auswählen, der über die Einladung schwebt.
- Dieses Update enthält Fehlerbehebungen und Leistungsverbesserungen.

### Update ist kostenfrei erhältlich

Da es sich um eine kostenlose App handelt, steht auch Version 1.13 ohne Aufpreis im App Store bereit. Wer selbst Einladungen verschicken möchte, sollte zwei Dinge beachten. Einerseits setzt die App ein iPhone mit iOS 26 oder neuer voraus, andererseits ist zum Erstellen von Veranstaltungen ein iCloud+-Abo nötig, das ab 0,99 Euro pro Monat erhältlich ist. Gäste können dagegen ohne Abo und von jedem Gerät aus antworten und abstimmen.

**[-> APPLE EINLADUNGEN LADEN](https://apps.apple.com/de/app/apple-einladungen/id6472498645?at=1000lIE4)**

items.articleBody:
From *Medium:*

“The purpose of life is self-development. To realise one’s natures perfectly. That is what each of us here for. People are afraid themselves now. They have forgotten that the highest of all duties. The duty that one owes to oneself. Think your natural thoughts, or burn with your natural passions. Have virtues that are real to you. Your own sins. Don’t be an actor in a part that isn’t written for you. Let life be your art. Set yourself to music, and your days will be sonnets. Resist it, and your soul grows sick with longing”.

While Wilde’s highlights the benefits of pursuing one’s goals through the tempting thrills and self-indulgence of aesthetic life, he warns us to be wary of its limits and dangers. Through Basil, Wilde cautions the dangers of submitting to the vices of our nature “my brains, such as they are – my art, whatever it may be worth; your rank and wealth, Harry; Dorian Gray’s good looks – we shall all suffer for what the gods have given us, suffer terribly”.

Dorian in his narcissism, has created a beautiful world for himself at the expense of others. One in which he indulges his passions, floating from one pursuit to the next; the study of perfumes, music, jewels, and embroideries, completely at his own whim. A life which, when I imagine a scenario where I am free from obligation, sounds appealing, wafting from one passion to the next. However, its Dorian’s passionate pursuit of pleasure over happiness, which causes him to become a monotonous and vain, indulgent in a never-ending stream of meaningless and trivial debaucher, using “evil as a mode through which he could realise his conception of the beautiful”.

More [↗ medium.com](https://medium.com/@gthepolymath/what-i-learned-from-the-picture-of-dorian-gray-by-oscar-wilde-1a72ffcb84d4).

items.articleBody:
Tirana, Albania, has become one of Europe’s fastest-growing cities. This growth has sparked a real estate boom, but locals worry about losing green areas and public spaces. Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG) has addressed these issues with its proposal for an upcoming development on Rinia Park, in the heart of Tirana.

Named Fountain Plaza Tirana, the project won over designs presented by four other international firms. Conceived as a mixed-use building, Fountain Plaza Tirana will stand several feet above Rinia Park, preserving and expanding the public park area while making room for a new hotel, apartments, offices, and cultural spaces.

The building evokes a dense cloud formation above the park. To achieve this, layers of rounded, perforated white terraces rest on slim columns, while two wider structures at opposite ends of the building house the elevators that provide floor access. To avoid breaking with the “floating” concept, these elements are clad in flute glass to let light shine through and onto the park.

“We have reimagined urban living in three dimensions—not as a vertical extrusion or a tower competing for attention on the skyline, but as a cloud of homes hovering above the park,” said BIG founder Bjarke Ingels told Dezeen. “Rather than diminishing the park or displacing public life, the building enhances and accommodates both.”

As such, Fountain Plaza Tirana will also feature an open-access library, a covered public auditorium, and community facilities. In addition to the design that lets pedestrians move freely across the park, this aims to make the building’s ground floor a bustling gathering place for city dwellers and visitors alike.

The design also accounts for Tirana’s weather, particularly its hot summers. The structures bring shade to a public park without completely blocking sunlight. Meanwhile, the water features, described as an “inverted fountain,” can cool the area with the effect of a light drizzle. The water used comes from a closed-loop system. With this, the water collected from the building and the green areas at the bottom is stored, filtered, and returned to the park below.

While a building timeline has yet to be announced, it will surely be interesting to see how Fountain Plaza Tirana takes shape. With time, resources, and care from the developers and the local government, it could become a cherished landmark in this fast-growing city, providing locals with a third space while welcoming visitors who want to experience a blooming Tirana firsthand.

Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG) won an international design competition for Fountain Plaza Tirana, a mixed-use development in the heart of Albania’s capital.

items.articleBody:
Framed by their car’s windshield, and then again by my rearview mirror, a man and a woman who seem to be a couple look like they'd rather be anywhere but together. He’s behind the wheel, doing all the talking; she’s looking straight ahead, motionless like a marble statue. Gradually, her face wears a desperate expression that only grows more hopeless as he continues talking and gesticulating.

In the supermarket checkout line, I pick up a copy of TIME magazine for the first time in God knows how long, drawn to a painting of Jesus Christ on the cover. It’s a special edition promising to tell us “Who he was. Who he is. His miracles, his mission, his love.” I expect to see a lot of biblical sheep inside, but I don’t find any. I buy the issue as an artifact. I stopped believing in TIME magazine a long time ago.

Down the street, a place that pretended to be a legitimate art gallery for a couple of months, showing the worst possible commercial art, has finally given up, and now it’s selling fur coats. A man in a cowboy hat walks past two girls dancing for a social media video. The air is chilly, and I think of buying myself a leather jacket.

And then I see her.

She looks at me with the most loving eyes as she holds a stack of perfectly folded laundry. She comforts me with her wide, auspicious smile, her jet-black hair, and her wrinkle-free, porcelain skin. I feel safe, accepted, and not judged. “Fast service, same day,” she promises because she’s just a model in an ad for a laundromat.

—Hakim Bishara, editor-in-chief

Mona Chalabi Paints a Picture of Class Inequality

“As an adult and as a journalist, I have stared shamelessly.” That refusal to look away is precisely what data journalist, writer, and artist Mona Chalabi has built her deeply principled career on. Known best for her indelible data visualizations, from the obscenity of Jeff Bezos’s wealth to the Israeli government’s starvation of Palestinians in Gaza and the racial and gender biases in museum collections, the Pulitzer Prize-winning Iraqi-British journalist tackles the subject of wealth and economic inequality in America in her first book, Ten Lives: How What We Have Shapes Who We Are (2026). | Lakshmi Rivera Amin

## Paramedic Receives Emotional Tribute From His Community After 59 Years on the Job

[↗ Primärquelle: mymodernmet.com](https://mymodernmet.com/paramedic-mike-nevill/)

> View this post on Instagram
> [A post shared by Region of Durham Paramedic Services (@durhamparamedic)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Deyk-IKJ747/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

Being a paramedic takes a special kind of person. It calls for compassion, resilience, and the ability to stay calm when others are at their most vulnerable. Just one day on the job can take its toll, yet Durham, California-based paramedic Mike Nevill dedicated an incredible 59 years to the vital role. A recent [viral video](https://www.instagram.com/p/Deyk-IKJ747/) captures a heartwarming tribute made to Nevill as he sits in his ambulance for the last time before retiring.

As Nevill sits in the driver’s seat, he listens to a radio tribute from the dispatch team thanking him for his dedication and reflecting on his extraordinary career. Outside the ambulance, community members gather to show their support, while Nevill appears visibly emotional. The tribute also highlights how Nevill inspired his own daughter to follow in his footsteps and become a paramedic, “carrying forward the Nevill family tradition of caring for others.”

When sharing the video on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Deyk-IKJ747/), Durham Region Paramedic Services wrote in the caption, “Beginning his career in 1967, Mike dedicated a lifetime to caring for others, serving as a paramedic, supervisor, mentor and leader. His commitment extended beyond Durham, with decades of service in Kawartha Lakes and Northumberland County as well.” They added, “The number of lives Mike has touched throughout his record-breaking career is truly immeasurable. Thank you for your dedication, compassion and commitment to our profession and community.”

People online were quick to share their admiration for Nevill’s decades of service. One person wrote, “59 years of service??? Paramedics have the hardest of all first responders, dude as a [Firefighter](https://mymodernmet.com/la-wildfire-firefighter-tribute/) my hat is off to you.” Another commented, “59 years as a paramedic! This man should never have to pay for a drink again.”

Let’s hope Nevill can now enjoy a well-deserved rest.

**Region of Durham Paramedic Services: [Website](https://www.durham.ca/living-here/emergency-services/ambulance-and-paramedics/) | [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/RegionofDurham/) | [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/durhamparamedic/)**

items.title: Could brain energy mismatches explain altered experiences in schizophrenia?
items.subtitle: A minute can seem shorter when you are having fun, yet it feels painfully long when you're bored or stressed.
items.feedText: Although this gap between actual time and perceived time is something we all experience, it can be much more pronounced in people with schizophrenia-spectrum conditions. They may experience time and space very differently from others, with time seeming fragmented, familiar surroundings feeling strange or disconnected, and even their sense of self shifting.

items.articleBody:
Sadie Stein in *The New York Times:*

As Herman Melville wrote, “Yes, there is death in this business of whaling — a speechlessly quick chaotic bundling of a man into Eternity.” Not everyone would read these words and think: cocktail bar. But for Bryan Schneider, the connection was obvious from the first time he read “Moby-Dick.” “I’m always reading from the bartender’s perspective,” he said. Schneider spent years tending bar for some of New York’s premier hospitality luminaries, Toby Cecchini, Julie Reiner and Daniel Boulud among them. All the while, he was thinking about Melville’s novel, which turns 175 this year.

Particularly inspiring was a description of a whalers’ watering hole called the Spouter-Inn, where the narrator, Ishmael, casts in his lot with the damned crew of the Pequod:

> Crossing this dusky entry, and on through yon low-arched way — cut through what in old times must have been a great central chimney with fireplaces all round — you enter the public room. A still duskier place is this, with such low ponderous beams above, and such old wrinkled planks beneath, that you would almost fancy you trod some old craft’s cockpits, especially of such a howling night, when this corner-anchored old ark rocked so furiously.

“I’d never read a vivid description like that before — so poetic,” Schneider said. “There were just so many cues for a bar! Yes,” he admits, “you could call it my white whale.”

More [↗ nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/14/books/moby-dick-book-club-quick-eternity.html?unlocked_article_code=1.QlE.-wTb.BlmAYGjiq4-e&smid=url-share).

items.articleBody:
**Das Licht einer vor rund 8,8 Milliarden Jahren explodierten Supernova könnte in gut 70 Jahren zweimal erneut die Erde erreichen. Ein Galaxienhaufen lenkt die Strahlung auf verschiedenen Wegen zu uns und erzeugt so zeitlich versetzte Bilder desselben Ereignisses. Diese Beobachtungen könnten künftig helfen, die Expansion des Universums genauer zu vermessen.**

**Baltimore (U.S.A.).** Für Menschen erscheinen Sternexplosionen wie einmalige Ereignisse, doch das Licht einer Supernova kann mehrfach und zu verschiedenen Zeiten am Himmel auftauchen. Möglich wird dies durch eine Gravitationslinse, bei der ein massereiches Objekt die Raumzeit krümmt und die Strahlung einer dahinterliegenden Quelle ablenkt.

Ein solcher Effekt vergrößert nicht nur weit entfernte Galaxien, sondern kann auch mehrere Bilder derselben Sternexplosion erzeugen. Weil die Lichtstrahlen unterschiedlich lange Wege durch die gekrümmte Raumzeit nehmen, treffen diese Bilder zu unterschiedlichen Zeiten auf der Erde ein.

### Fernste Supernova ihrer Art

Forscher des Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI) um Conor Larison haben die Supernova SN Ares hinter dem Galaxienhaufen MACS J0308.9+2645 untersucht. Entdeckt wurde sie am 23. August 2025 in Infrarotaufnahmen des James-Webb-Weltraumteleskops, die eine weit entfernte, durch die Gravitationslinse dreifach abgebildete Galaxie zeigen.

Von der Supernova selbst ist bislang nur eines dieser möglichen Bilder zu sehen. Die anderen Lichtwege führen nach den Berechnungen des Teams zu zwei späteren Abbildungen, die noch nicht bei der Erde angekommen sind.

Spektren aus weiteren Webb-Beobachtungen zeigen charakteristische Linien von Wasserstoff und Helium. Diese sprechen für eine Kernkollaps-Supernova vom Typ IIb, bei der ein massereicher Stern vor der Explosion den Großteil seiner äußeren Wasserstoffhülle verloren hat.

> „Starke Gravitationslinsen verwandeln Galaxienhaufen in die leistungsfähigsten Teleskope der Natur“, erklärt Seiji Fujimoto von der University of Toronto.

Mit einer Rotverschiebung von z = 1,276 ist SN Ares nach der Analyse die bislang am weitesten entfernte spektroskopisch identifizierte Supernova dieser Klasse. Die Untersuchung wurde am 23. Oktober 2026 als wissenschaftlicher Preprint veröffentlicht und ist bisher nicht fachbegutachtet.

### Weitere Bilder erst um das Jahr 2100

Für die Zeitvorhersage hat das Team drei unabhängige Modelle der Massenverteilung im Vordergrundhaufen verglichen. Ihre Ergebnisse liegen nicht genau übereinander, erwarten aber die beiden weiteren Bilder etwa 70 bis 79 Jahre nach der bereits beobachteten Erscheinung.

Ein Modell berechnet Verzögerungen von rund 70 und 73 Jahren, ein zweites von 72 und 77 Jahren. Das dritte kommt auf ungefähr 76 und 79 Jahre, sodass die häufig genannten 73 und 76 Jahre keine festen Beobachtungstermine sind.

Zudem hängen die vorausgesagten Ankunftszeiten von der angenommenen kosmischen Expansionsrate ab. Schon vergleichsweise kleine Änderungen dieses Modellwerts können die berechneten Laufzeiten um mehrere Jahre verschieben.

Die künftigen Bilder könnten durch den Galaxienhaufen ungefähr fünf- beziehungsweise anderthalbfach verstärkt erscheinen. Ob sie sich dann tatsächlich nachweisen lassen, wird auch von den verfügbaren Teleskopen und der Genauigkeit der vorherigen Modellrechnungen abhängen.

### Eine Messuhr für das Universum

Gerade die ungewöhnlich lange Verzögerung könnte sich für die Kosmologie als wertvoll erweisen. Die Zeitabstände zwischen den verschiedenen Lichtwegen hängen von der Geometrie des Linsensystems und den Entfernungen im expandierenden Universum ab.

Falls die beiden Bilder tatsächlich eintreffen, ließen sich ihre Ankunftszeiten sehr präzise bestimmen und zur Messung der Hubble-Konstante nutzen. Diese Größe beschreibt die gegenwärtige Expansionsrate des Universums und ist Gegenstand voneinander abweichender astronomischer Messungen.

Eine äußerst genaue Messung der Verzögerung allein würde allerdings noch keine ebenso genaue Bestimmung der Hubble-Konstante garantieren. Die größte verbleibende Unsicherheit könnte in der Beschreibung der Massenverteilung des Galaxienhaufens liegen.

Für Anfang 2027 sind zusätzliche spektroskopische Beobachtungen der mehrfach abgebildeten Hintergrundobjekte vorgesehen. Sie sollen die Linsenmodelle verbessern und die Zeitfenster für die beiden noch erwarteten Supernovabilder genauer eingrenzen.

**Quellen:**

- Forschungs-Preprint auf [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33161), doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2610.33161
- Offizielle Studienmitteilung von [Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources](https://jwst-venus.github.io/news/news_20260107.html) (VENUS)

items.articleBody:
## Sure Presence

When wood goes through transformation

and becomes fire, we feel some sure presence

behind the flame that may burn out soon, a

sure presence that comes to us with certainty.

On this fire we cook to eat and

exchange our presence.

It was in that friendship circle gathering that

humans began burning offerings to God,

offering their food cooked on that fire.

That sense of sure presence, felt through history,

was shared by fishermen at the sea of Galilee.

That sure presence is with us now in substance,

in the material world within and around us.

*By Lucien Miller* *from* [The Hidden Side of the Mountain](https://fonsvitae.com/product/the-hidden-side-of-the-mountain-encounters-with-wisdoms-poor-holy/) *Fons Vitae, Louisville, KY, 2021*

items.articleBody:
This leather shoe was discovered in Areni 1 cave during excavations in 2008.

Made from a single piece of cowhide leather, and still with its leather laces it has been measured as corresponding to a modern US size 7 / EU size 37 / UK size 6. It is stuffed with grass to either maintain its shape or keep the foot warm. It is unknown at this stage whether it was a man or woman's shoe.

Researchers have managed to date it back to 3600-3500 BC based on the radiocarbon dating.

The shoe managed to survive in near-perfect condition because of the cool, dry cave environment which was sealed off by several layers of sheep dung. The shoe was found upside down at the base of a shallow, rounded, and plastered pit, beneath an overturned broken Chalcolithic ceramic bowl.

items.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
items.subtitle: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of bi…

items.articleBody:
A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times.

[Comet](https://www.space.com/comets.html) [220P/McNaught](https://www.space.com/astronomy/comets/comet-mcnaught-put-on-a-surprise-show-this-summer-heres-how-to-spot-it-before-it-fades) was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the [sun](https://www.space.com/58-the-sun-formation-facts-and-characteristics.html) as [Mars](https://www.space.com/astronomy/solar-system/mars). Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year.

On June 14, as it headed towards [perihelion](https://www.space.com/what-is-perihelion) – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an [astronomical unit)](https://www.space.com/17081-how-far-is-earth-from-the-sun.html), 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life.

On 31 May, the comet was languishing at [magnitude](https://www.space.com/21640-star-luminosity-and-magnitude.html) +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes.

## Telling the tale of a dirty snowball

Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space.

Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten.

"We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a [statement](https://ice.csic.es/news/news-press-releases?view=article&id=1072:an-international-collaboration-obtains-the-most-accurate-measurement-of-the-expansion-of-the-universe-2&catid=8).

Comet 220P/McNaught imaged from an observatory in Spain on 7 August following its second outburst. (Image credit: Peter Carson.)

While this is the first time that 220P has been seen to outburst, over the years we have witnessed other comets spectacularly brighten out of nowhere.

A recent and well-known example is comet [17P/Holmes](https://www.space.com/comet-holmes-debris-could-reveal-secrets), which brightened a million-fold in the fall of 2007 as it rose from magnitude +17 to magnitude +2.8, becoming a welcome naked-eye sight in the constellation of [Perseus](https://www.space.com/perseus-constellation.html) for many people as they made the evening commute home.

The short 5.5-year orbit of 220P marks it out as a [Jupiter](https://www.space.com/7-jupiter-largest-planet-solar-system.html)-family comet.

"Jupiter-family comets are extremely interesting objects to study because they originate primarily from the [Kuiper Belt](https://www.space.com/16144-kuiper-belt-objects.html) and the Scattered Disk region, later migrating inward until Jupiter captures them into short-period orbits," said Trigo-Rodríguez.

Studying outbursts such as the two experienced by 220P provides vital clues as to the bulk characteristics of Jupiter-family comets, giving us insight into objects that originated from beyond the orbit of [Neptune](https://www.space.com/41-neptune-the-other-blue-planet-in-our-solar-system.html).

An illustration of a comet approaching Earth. (Image credit: Robert Lea)

Of particular interest to Trigo-Rodríguez is what we should do were one of these objects ever to be found on a collision course with [Earth](https://www.space.com/54-earth-history-composition-and-atmosphere.html).

"Particularly we are interested in the tensile strength and nature of comets in the framework of our studies on impact hazards," said Trigo-Rodríguez. "Some comets seem determined to demonstrate that they are fragile enough and perhaps give us the chance to invoke disruptive approaches that might be substantially different from the ones already tested or proposed for asteroids."

For now, 220P is heading back out to its furthest point from the sun, which is just inside the orbit of Jupiter at a distance of 4.68 astronomical units or 435 million miles (700 million kilometers). Having passed as close to Earth as it is going to get this time around on 12 October at a distance of 1.04 astronomical units or 97 million miles (156 million kilometres), the comet is currently magnitude +13 and fading. All eyes will be on 220P during its next time around the sun in late 2031.

The findings were published on Nov.3 in the [Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://academic.oup.com/mnras/article/553/1/stag1814/9003544?login=false).

items.title: ‘The Sacred Ordinary’ Shines a Light on Heritage in Birmingham’s Civil Rights District
items.subtitle: In the second stanza of “How to Be a Poet,” Wendell Berry wrote: “There are no unsacred places; / there are only sacred places / and desecrated pla…
items.feedText: The participatory artwork is presented in collaboration with the National Parks Conservation Association, which aims to protect U.S. national parks for future generations. In early 2025, President Trump issued an executive order that mandated the removal of some National Park Service signage relating to slavery, the LGBTQ+ community, climate change, and more, a move that erases histories inextricable from the nation’s identity. items.articleBody:
In the second stanza of “How to Be a Poet,” Wendell Berry wrote: “There are no unsacred places; / there are only sacred places / and desecrated places.” When it comes to preserving important historical locations, such as monuments, parks, and buildings, a new interactive public art installation asks, “what happens when preservation itself is endangered?”

The Sacred Ordinary is an initiative organized by 1504, a production studio based in Birmingham that emphasizes in-depth storytelling to connect people with meaningful, human-focused services and experiences. The participatory artwork is presented in collaboration with the National Parks Conservation Association, which aims to protect U.S. national parks for future generations.

In early 2025, President Trump issued an executive order that mandated the removal of some National Park Service signage relating to slavery, the LGBTQ+ community, climate change, and more, a move that erases histories inextricable from the nation’s identity. (The current administration has also blocked millions in funding for numerous parks and disrupted services.)

In Birmingham, the Civil Rights District is formally designated a national monument, comprising neighborhoods that Black people historically called home and where Jim Crow laws authorized segregation until the 1960s. The Civil Rights Movement reached a nexus here when activists Fred Shuttlesworth, Martin Luther King, Jr., and Ralph Abernathy, among many others, organized nonviolent marches in 1963, known today as the Birmingham Campaign. Police turned their dogs on demonstrators and used fire hoses on children. A bombing at a Baptist church killed four young Black girls.

The Sacred Ordinary venerates access to things most of us take for granted: the ability to shop at any store, attend the nearest school, walk around any neighborhood, and sit at the front of the bus. The exhibition is installed around-the-clock, but by day, elements of the installation comprise vintage yet mundane objects that one typically walks by without giving a second thought.

A huge midcentury television rests on an open lawn, and a red newspaper vending box for The Birmingham News, which ceased its print publication in 2012, advertises 25 cents per copy. Additional sites include a characteristically blue U.S. Postal Service mailbox and a walk-in telephone booth. Sheets of paper with tear-off tabs posted around town invite participants to learn more by texting a phone number. If you text “HERE” to the number, you’ll be directed to a starting point and an otherwise nondescript yellow fire hydrant.

In scavenger-hunt style, visitors are prompted to enter the year stamped on the unit, and if it’s between 5 and 8 p.m., the sequence of texted prompts doubles as a multimedia self-guided tour of Birmingham’s Civil Rights District like you’ve never seen it: the television screen, mailbox, phone booth, and more begin to glow once the sun has set.

“Birmingham, Alabama, is known around the world for such places—sites of civil rights history that many regard as sacred and that connect us to something larger than ourselves. But today, that memory is endangered,” 1504 says in a statement. “Aging infrastructure, the passing of a generation of foot soldiers, and federal efforts to erase chapters of American history raise an urgent question: if institutions alone cannot sustain history, what role can the public play in caring for sacred sites?”

Rather than center primarily on signage, The Sacred Ordinary focuses on objects associated with civic life in the mid-20th century, evoking collective memories and providing touchpoints for younger generations for whom boxy televisions, printed newspapers, and telephone booths feel distant from today’s experiences. Emblematic of the way news and information spread before the internet and smartphones, the objects confront visitors with not only the realities of how people organized and communicated during that time but also how those memories are preserved today. Even without didactics, objects and places carry meaning that no one can simply delete.

The tour opens with a narration by actor André Holland, who played a fundamental role in preserving a historic theater in nearby Bessemer, Alabama, and 1504 has dedicated the installation to Birmingham-based artist Joe Minter. The Sacred Ordinary continues nightly through December 13, with accompanying guided walks and other programs scheduled in the meantime. Learn more on the project’s website, and explore the studio’s work on Instagram. You might also be interested in “The Praise House,” directed by 1504’s Tyler Jones.

items.articleBody:
Der [Apple Pencil Pro](https://www.ifun.de/amzn/B0D3J7CKFR) kostet bei Amazon aktuell 99 Euro und erreicht damit seinen niedrigsten Preis innerhalb der vergangenen 365 Tage. Gegenüber Apples unverbindlicher Preisempfehlung von 149 Euro entspricht das einem Nachlass von rund 34 Prozent.

#### Beeindruckende ProCreate-Skizzen von Paraph14

[↗ Primärquelle: x.com](https://x.com/Paraph14/status/2113505300867362844)

## Pro-Funktionen für das iPad

Der Apple Pencil Pro ist das am besten ausgestattete Modell in Apples Stiftangebot. Er berücksichtigt beim Zeichnen sowohl den ausgeübten Druck als auch die Neigung. Hinzu kommen eine Rotationserkennung, haptische Rückmeldungen und die Einbindung in Apples „Wo ist?“-Netzwerk. Diese Funktionen unterscheiden ihn vom einfacheren USB-C-Modell und machen ihn vor allem für Nutzer interessant, die regelmäßig zeichnen oder illustrieren.

#### Oben der Apple Pencil Pro, unten das USB-C-Modell

Passende Software gibt es inzwischen auch ohne Kaufpreis: Die kürzlich [veröffentlichte iPad-Version von Affinity](https://www.ifun.de/affinity-fuer-ipad-ist-da-bildbearbeitung-und-layout-kostenlos-293956/) kombiniert Bildbearbeitung, Vektorgrafik und Layout. Sie unterstützt die Sonderfunktionen des Apple Pencil und kann beim Zeichnen Druck und Neigung berücksichtigen.

Produkthinweis

[Apple Pencil Pro: Fortschrittliche Tools, pixelgenaue Präzision, Neigungs und Drucksensitivität und branchenführende...](https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0D3J7CKFR?tag=musicweb02&linkCode=ogi&th=1&psc=1)
99,00 EUR
149,00 EUR

## Beim iPhone Duo hilft nur USB-C

Wer auf dem iPhone Duo zeichnen möchte, muss trotz der umfangreicheren Ausstattung des Pro zum einfacheren Apple Pencil mit USB-C greifen. Apples faltbares iPhone unterstützt ausschließlich dieses Modell. Das gilt auch nach der inzwischen nachgereichten Stiftfreigabe, wie wir [in unserem Alltagstest](https://www.iphone-ticker.de/iphone-duo-im-test-das-beste-ipad-ist-jetzt-ein-iphone-289952/) festhalten. Der Apple Pencil Pro besitzt keinen USB-C-Anschluss und lädt induktiv. Am Duo bleibt er außen vor.

#### Per Kabelverbindung lädt das iPhone Duo den Apple Pencil | Video: chehonz201

[↗ Primärquelle: x.com](https://x.com/chehonz201/status/2115687570130850018)

Der USB-C-Stift lässt sich dagegen per Kabel direkt am iPhone Duo aufladen. Zum Nachladen ist damit kein separates Netzteil erforderlich. Auf beiden Displays kann er für handschriftliche Notizen, Skizzen und Anmerkungen in Dokumenten eingesetzt werden.

Das passende [USB-C-Modell](https://www.ifun.de/amzn/B0CL7DZXB2) ist derzeit für 79,99 Euro erhältlich. Laut Amazons Preisangaben ist das der niedrigste Stand der vergangenen 30 Tage. items.articleBody:
Using anonymized credit card data, Bloomberg illustrated a three-year timeline of online gambling. As a backdrop, Bloomberg identified people who made their first transaction with an online sportsbook in Massachusetts, when it was legalized in the state.

Because legalized online sports gambling is a relatively new phenomenon in the US, few studies have been able to measure its impact beyond high-level, aggregate statistics. But in other countries, academics have been able to run robust, yearslong analyses. The 2021 study out of the UK used individual-level transaction data from 6.5 million customers of Lloyds Banking Group, or 10.6% of the country’s population, over a course of seven years. The study paints a dark picture: The more money people spend gambling online, the worse their financial situation.

The consequences extend into their personal lives too. They spend less time on hobbies, education and social activities. They travel and exercise less. They’re more likely to spend their nights awake.

It’s hard to separate causation and correlation in a lot of the examples. People who are likely to miss a loan payment are probably likely to gamble a lot, because money management is not a forte overall. So while we don’t know that online gambling brings a bunch of problems, it is likely that having a casino in your pocket does not help the situation.

## Audible-Aktion: 3 Monate je 0,99 Euro + 15 Euro Guthaben geschenkt

Kürzlich hat Amazon die [Black Friday Woche 2026](https://link.amazon/B01GgT9IU) für den 19. bis 30 November angekündigt. Verschiedene Aktionen starten allerdings bereits im Vorfeld. Ab sofort und zeitlich befristet könnt ihr euch [Audible drei Monate für je 0,99 Euro sichern](https://link.amazon/A09Eaek5z). Auf diese Art und Weise könnt ihr euch jeden Monat 1 Hörbuch aus dem gesamten Audible-Katalog (über 900.000 Titel) auswählen. Ihr könnt eure ausgewählten Hörbücher hören, solange ihr Audible-Mitglied seid. Darüberhinaus habt ihr natürlich die Option, zusätzliche Hörbücher zum vollen Preis zu kaufen. Darüber hinaus habt ihr kostenlosen Zugriff auf beliebige Podcasts.

Der 15 Euro Audible-Gutschein wird als Gutschein in eurem Konto angezeigt. Er wird beim Kauf eines berechtigten Titels automatisch an der Kasse eingelöst. Ihr könnt eure verfügbaren Gutscheine auch in den Kontodetails einsehen.

Nach Ablauf der 3 Monate, in denen ihr nur 0,99 Euro monatlich bezahlt, steigt der monatliche Preis für Audible Standard auf 6,99 Euro. Das „Probe-Abo“ ist allerdings jederzeit kündbar, so dass ihr nach Ablauf der drei reduzierten Monate „aussteigen“ könnt.

items.subtitle:

items.articleBody:
From [the Archive](https://marginalrevolution.com/ai-archive/), written by ChatGPT:

**The clearest standouts are Loveless, Brazil Classics 1, Solo Monk, and the Louvin Brothers’ Tragic Songs of Life. Bach receives the strongest sustained endorsement across the years.** Some of these recommendations were buried in country profiles and assorted links rather than music posts.

This selection draws on the Marginal Revolution archive from 2003 through October 2026, giving greatest weight to explicit all-time praise, repeated endorsements, and evidence of continued listening. It assesses the strength of Cowen’s recommendations; it is not a ranking he himself published. Dates below refer to his posts.

Amazon links are affiliate links. Editions and availability may vary.

## 1. My Bloody Valentine — Loveless

> “Certainly my favorite album post-1970s, and possibly my favorite of all time.”

That is about as strong an album endorsement as the archive yields. It puts his enthusiasm for experimental popular music alongside his devotion to classical music. His praise for the band’s later *mbv* reinforces that this was a continuing attachment.

**Source:** [March 11, 2017 — “My favorite things Ireland”](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2017/03/favorite-things-ireland.html). His praise for *mbv* appears in [“Favorite popular music 2013,” December 15, 2013](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2013/12/favorite-popular-music-2013.html).

**Amazon:** [Loveless — vinyl reissue](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B091GLSHHQ?tag=marginalrevol-20); [mbv](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00BHUJ2XI?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 2. Various artists, selected by David Byrne — Brazil Classics 1

> “sometimes I feel it is my favorite CD period.”

He also places it among his ten desert-island discs. Especially revealing: Cowen thinks Brazilian popular music often works better as selected songs than as individual artists’ albums, so this compilation is his preferred introduction to an exceptionally rich musical tradition.

**Source:** [December 28, 2006 — “My favorite things Brazil, music edition”](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2006/12/my_favorite_thi.html).

**Amazon:** [Brazil Classics 1: Beleza Tropical](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0000DB51P?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 3. Thelonious Monk — Solo Monk

> “My number one pick is Thelonious Monk’s Solo Monk”

This is his explicit first choice in an early discussion of the greatest jazz albums. Five years later, he again calls it “my favorite jazz album?” That repetition makes it a particularly solid recommendation. The original post also singles out Sun Ra and Cecil Taylor’s *Silent Tongues*.

**Sources:** [October 5, 2003](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2003/10/the_15_greatest.html); [May 14, 2008](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2008/05/the-100-best-ja.html).

**Amazon:** [Solo Monk](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0000AVHBN?tag=marginalrevol-20); [Cecil Taylor — Silent Tongues](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07J35QCHJ?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 4. The Louvin Brothers — Tragic Songs of Life

> “one of my favorite recordings of all time, any genre.”

This is an unusually unequivocal endorsement. He had already recommended it in 2008 and 2009; in the latter post, he emphasizes its unsettling, tragic character and argues that listeners can love it even if they ordinarily dislike country and bluegrass.

**Sources:** [January 26, 2011](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2011/01/charlie-louvin-has-passed-away-at-83.html); [July 17, 2009 — “My favorite things Alabama”](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2009/07/my-favorite-things-alabama.html).

**Amazon:** [Tragic Songs of Life](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00009UVZP?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 5. Bach — The Art of the Fugue, played by Grigory Sokolov

> “Best of all is the Art of the Fugue, for piano, by Grigory Sokolov.”

This comes within a detailed selection of essential Bach recordings, making “best of all” particularly significant. Cowen had also endorsed the recording in 2005 while discussing Thomas Schelling’s affection for it. For a single classical recommendation with both emphatic language and longevity, this is one of the strongest.

**Sources:** [March 25, 2007 — “My favorite things German: J.S. Bach”](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2007/03/my_favorite_thi_2.html); [October 10, 2005](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2005/10/facts_about_tho.html).

**Amazon:** [Sokolov — Bach: The Art of the Fugue](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00005RCZ5?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 6. Bach — Benjamin Alard’s keyboard recordings and Masaaki Suzuki’s cantatas

On Alard:

> “These are some of the best recordings of the best music I have heard, ever.”

He calls Alard his biggest discovery of 2022. Suzuki receives similarly exceptional praise: in 2020 Cowen describes his complete cantata cycle as definitive, and the cycle remains prominent in his 2024 listening. These recommendations show that his Bach enthusiasm keeps generating new discoveries.

**Sources:** [November 27, 2022](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2022/11/what-i-listened-to-in-2022.html); [November 15, 2020](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2020/11/best-classical-music-recordings-of-2020.html); [November 29, 2024](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2024/11/classical-music-listening-for-the-year.html).

**Amazon:** [Alard — The Complete Works for Keyboard, Volume 1](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07923JSCD?tag=marginalrevol-20) (an entry point to the series, not the complete collection); [Suzuki and Bach Collegium Japan — Complete Sacred Cantatas, 55-disc Japanese edition](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00IODK18G?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 7. Bola Sete — Samba in Seattle: Live at the Penthouse 1966–1968; Doc Watson — Life’s Work: A Retrospective

He describes these two sets as:

> “some of the best guitar recordings of all time.”

Sete receives the greater individual emphasis: Cowen judges the release’s contribution and historical importance across all musical genres. His admiration for Sete was already explicit in 2006, fifteen years earlier. Watson’s set is also judged substantially better than other Watson collections.

**Sources:** [December 10, 2021](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2021/12/the-best-guitar-music-from-2021.html); [December 28, 2006](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2006/12/my_favorite_thi.html).

**Amazon:** [Bola Sete — Samba in Seattle](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09HV24S1P?tag=marginalrevol-20); [Doc Watson — Life’s Work: A Retrospective](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09FGV1VS1?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 8. Beethoven — piano sonatas played by Yves Nat; complete piano music played by Martino Tirimo

On Nat:

> “it stands as one of my desert island discs.”

Cowen values Nat’s directness and depth. Fifteen years later, Tirimo’s complete Beethoven piano recordings enter his two or three favorite sets ever. These are especially useful recommendations because he identifies particular performers after comparing interpretations, rather than merely recommending Beethoven.

**Sources:** [February 6, 2005](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2005/02/my_favorite_thi.html); [November 15, 2020](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2020/11/best-classical-music-recordings-of-2020.html).

**Amazon:** [Yves Nat — Beethoven piano sonatas](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000002S0L?tag=marginalrevol-20); [Martino Tirimo — Beethoven: Complete Piano Works](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07W8LJNQ1?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 9. Cécile McLorin Salvant — Dreams and Daggers, Ghost Song, and Mélusine

> “Her track record (and consistency) at this point is simply staggering”

This is one of the strongest sustained recommendations of a contemporary performer. He recommends her work in 2013, calls her the new Ella Fitzgerald in 2017, includes *Ghost Song* in 2022, and places her alongside the greatest female jazz vocalists in 2023. **Start with Dreams and Daggers or Mélusine.**

**Sources:** [August 15, 2013](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2013/08/what-ive-been-listening-to-2.html); [December 24, 2017](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2017/12/favorite-jazz-2017.html); [December 18, 2022](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2022/12/popular-music-recommendations-for-2022.html); [November 27, 2023](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2023/11/my-favorite-non-classical-music-of-the-year-2023.html).

**Amazon:** [Dreams and Daggers](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B073LJT75M?tag=marginalrevol-20); [Ghost Song](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09KNCY5F3?tag=marginalrevol-20); [Mélusine](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BSRN3VGF?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 10. Mozart — the operas, particularly Don Giovanni conducted by Teodor Currentzis

> “If I had to choose the operas, or all the rest of Mozart put together, I would go for the operas.”

That establishes the strength of his preference within Mozart. Currentzis’s *Don Giovanni* wins his top classical-recording prize for 2016, and he returns to it approvingly in 2021.

**Sources:** [August 7, 2017](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2017/08/favorite-things-austria-wolfgang-amadeus-mozart.html); [January 10, 2017](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2017/01/best-classical-music-recordings-2016.html); [December 27, 2021](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2021/12/favorite-classical-music-of-the-year.html).

**Amazon:** [Currentzis — Mozart: Don Giovanni](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01L5WLRXU?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 11. Andrés Segovia — Bach recordings

> “some of the best musical interpretations of Bach by anyone playing any instrument.”

The breadth of that comparison makes this much stronger than a recommendation for guitar enthusiasts. Cowen treats these recordings as permanent additions to a collection.

**Source:** [February 20, 2008](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2008/02/my-favorite-thi.html).

**Amazon:** [The Segovia Collection, Volume 1: The Legendary Andrés Segovia in an All-Bach Program](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000002PGS?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## 12. Bruckner — the symphony cycle conducted by Marek Janowski

> “the best Bruckner overall.”

This is a particularly strong recent recommendation, backed by his explicit comparison with numerous competing recordings. It also demonstrates that his preferred classical performances continue to change.

**Source:** [March 9, 2026](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2026/03/recent-recordings-of-big-symphonies.html).

**Amazon:** [Janowski and Orchestre de la Suisse Romande — Bruckner: Complete Symphonies](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CMDJ32KS?tag=marginalrevol-20).

## Strong endorsements from the annual listening posts

His annual listening posts add several emphatic recommendations worth distinguishing from those all-time judgments.

## What the recommendations reveal

The most revealing pattern is **the combination of repeat listening and highly specific performances**. His strongest recommendations often concern a particular interpretation, compilation, or recovered concert recording. And his clearest statement about actual listening habits is simple:**“Bach gets the most listening time.”** [February 26, 2024 — “How I listen to music”](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2024/02/how-i-listen-to-music.html).

items.articleBody:
**Lauschangriff aus dem Meeresboden: Ein Telekommunikationskabel vor Alaska hat nach Angaben der beteiligten Forschungseinrichtung erstmals Rufe von Grönlandwalen registriert. Bisher gelang der Nachweis über solche Leitungen vor allem bei besonders tief rufenden Blau- und Finnwalen. Der neue Versuch deutet darauf hin, dass die Glasfasertechnik künftig ein breiteres Spektrum von Meeressäugern erfassen könnte.**

**Ithaca (U.S.A.).** Unterseeische Glasfaserkabel transportieren normalerweise Daten zwischen Orten, die viele Kilometer voneinander entfernt liegen. Doch die dünnen Glasfasern reagieren auch auf minimale Dehnungen, wenn Schallwellen aus dem Wasser die Kabel und den Meeresboden in Schwingung versetzen. Diese Eigenschaft lässt sich für eine Art unsichtbares Unterwasser-Lauschnetz nutzen.

Die sogenannte verteilte akustische Messung, englisch Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS), liefert entlang eines Kabels viele virtuelle Messstellen. Anders als bei einzelnen Unterwassermikrofonen entstehen so räumlich zugeordnete Signale über Dutzende Kilometer, die sich vom Land aus auslesen lassen. Das könnte gerade bei der Überwachung von Walen in schwer zugänglichen Meeresgebieten helfen.

### Erstmals höhere Walrufe im Kabelsignal

Im Frühjahr 2026 hat die Bioakustikerin Léa Bouffaut von der Cornell University bei Utqiaġvik an Alaskas Nordküste Messungen an einer bestehenden Glasfaserleitung durchgeführt. Das Kabel gehört zum nordalaskanischen Netz des Telekommunikationsunternehmens Quintillion, das auch Utqiaġvik versorgt. Bei den Arbeiten kooperierte sie mit örtlichen Walfangvertretern und der regionalen Wildtierbehörde.

Das Ziel war anspruchsvoller als bei früheren Versuchen: Grönlandwale rufen häufig in Frequenzbereichen um 150 bis 300 Hertz und vergleichsweise leise. Dagegen hatten Glasfaserkabel zuvor vor allem die lauteren Rufe von Blau- und Finnwalen mit Frequenzen unter 100 Hertz erfasst. Nach wochenlanger Auswertung von Terabytes an Daten wurden nun erstmals Grönlandwalrufe in solchen Glasfasermessungen erkannt, wie Cornell berichtet.

> „Es ist entscheidend, dass wir jetzt den immensen Wert dieser Kabel für Naturschutz und Betrieb nachweisen“, erklärt Léa Bouffaut.

Der neue Grönlandwalnachweis ist bislang nur in einer offiziellen Forschungsmitteilung beschrieben. Eine gesonderte begutachtete Originalstudie mit Messprotokoll, Nachweisrate und statistischer Auswertung dieser Aufzeichnungen ließ sich dafür bislang nicht ermitteln. Aus dem berichteten Nachweis lässt sich daher noch nicht ableiten, wie zuverlässig die Methode andere Bartenwale unter unterschiedlichen Bedingungen erfasst.

### Ein Kabel, Tausende Messpunkte

Das Messprinzip beruht auf Laserpulsen, die ein spezielles Gerät in die Glasfaser schickt und deren zurückgestreutes Licht es analysiert. Schallwellen verändern die Faser minimal, wodurch sich die Laufzeit beziehungsweise Phase des zurücklaufenden Lichts messbar verschiebt. Aus diesen Veränderungen entstehen viele virtuelle Sensoren entlang der Leitung, die Walrufe räumlich eingrenzen können.

Wie leistungsfähig das sein kann, zeigte bereits eine 2022 veröffentlichte Untersuchung an Spitzbergen. Dort wurden Gesänge von Blau- und Finnwalen entlang einer 120 Kilometer langen Unterwasserleitung erfasst. Spätere Untersuchungen mit zwei parallelen Kabeln ermöglichten es, mehrere Finnwale gleichzeitig zu verfolgen und ihre Position unter den getesteten Bedingungen auf ungefähr 100 Meter einzugrenzen.

### Warum die Kabel nicht alles hören

Die Messungen sind kein Ersatz für gewöhnliche Unterwassermikrofone. Zwar können bestehende Leitungen lange Strecken überwachen, doch die tatsächliche Empfindlichkeit hängt unter anderem von der Kabelführung, ihrer Ummantelung und dem Meeresboden ab. Auch hohe Frequenzen und leise Rufe lassen sich mit typischen Telekommunikationskabeln bislang schlechter nachweisen als tiefe, laute Signale.

Hinzu kommt ein geometrisches Problem: Ein geradliniges Einzelkabel lässt meist offen, auf welcher Seite ein rufender Wal schwimmt. Mehrere Kabel oder gekrümmte Leitungsabschnitte können diese Mehrdeutigkeit verringern. Und die Datenmenge ist enorm: Bei 50 Kilometern Kabellänge, vier Metern Abstand zwischen den Messstellen, 2.000 Messungen pro Sekunde und zwei Byte pro Messwert fallen rechnerisch etwa 4,3 Terabyte täglich an.

### Mehr Wissen über Wale, aber noch keine Routine

In ihrer jüngst veröffentlichten wissenschaftlichen Übersichtsarbeit bündelt Bouffaut die bisherigen Einsätze der Technik und nennt die nächsten Entwicklungsschritte. Benötigt werden vergleichbare Tests für verschiedene Walarten und Kabeltypen, automatisierte Verfahren zur Erkennung der Rufe und Regeln für den Umgang mit großen sowie möglicherweise sensiblen Datensätzen. Erst damit ließen sich Nachweiswahrscheinlichkeit und Reichweite so bestimmen, dass Naturschutzmaßnahmen zuverlässig darauf aufbauen können.

Eine mögliche Anwendung wäre, wandernde Wale früher zu erkennen und Schifffahrt oder lärmintensive Arbeiten besser auf ihre Anwesenheit abzustimmen. Noch handelt es sich jedoch um eine Perspektive, nicht um ein flächendeckend einsatzbereites Frühwarnsystem. Die Beobachtung aus Alaska zeigt vor allem, dass ein bisher schwer erfassbarer Frequenzbereich zumindest unter bestimmten Bedingungen erreichbar sein könnte.

**Quellen:**

- Originalstudie im Fachmagazin [Frontiers in Marine Science](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2022.901348/full), doi: 10.3389/fmars.2022.901348
- Originalstudie im Fachmagazin [Frontiers in Marine Science](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2023.1130898/full), doi: 10.3389/fmars.2023.1130898
- Offizielle Studienmitteilung von [Cornell University](https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2026/11/repurposing-internets-backbone-advance-whale-monitoring)
- Offizielle Unternehmensquelle von [Quintillion](https://quintillionglobal.com/system-in-alaska/)
